title: Unit – 5 : Session – 10 : SLO – 2  |  LDM/STM and RISC vs CISC
sections: 1. C) STM — Store Multiple saves a block of registers to memory.
2. B) RISC — RISC architectures typically use fixed-length instructions.
3. B) Write-back — '!' updates the base register after the transfer.
2. variable-length — CISC uses variable instruction size.
3. stack — STMFD (Store Multiple Full Descending) is the standard stack-push operation.
2. FALSE — CISC supports more addressing modes than RISC.
3. TRUE — write-back ('!') updates the base register automatically.
3. STMFD SP!, {R1–R3} with SP = 0x1000: a full-descending push of 3 words decreases SP by 12 → new SP = 0x0FF4 (data stored at 0x0FF4–0x0FFF).
